text:
A 7-3 final in Calgary hid a game that was close to a coin flip. Colorado and Calgary created almost identical chances (2.83 expected goals for COL, 2.79 for CGY), and the simulated replays gave COL a 51 percent share of wins to CGY's 49. The gap came from the net. Devin Cooley allowed 4.2 more goals than the 30 shots he faced should have produced, while Scott Wedgewood stopped 26 of 29.

Devon Toews scored first for COL on a 13 percent tip-in at 15:54 of the first, and Adam Klapka answered for CGY 96 seconds later. The middle period tilted slightly toward the Flames on chance quality (1.27 to 1.05), yet COL scored three times in under five minutes. Toews put a wrist shot past Cooley at 6:45 on a 1 percent chance, the least likely goal of the night. Cale Makar and Nathan MacKinnon followed at 9:16 and 11:39, each on a 6 percent look, and COL led 4-1 without having controlled the period.

COL did own the third, out-chancing CGY 1.10 to 0.59, and Makar and Jaden Schwartz scored in a 59-second span to make it 6-1. CGY pulled back with goals from Mikael Backlund at 7:17 and Kevin Bahl at 8:28, but Schwartz restored the four-goal margin at 9:41. Makar finished with two goals and an assist, MacKinnon with a goal and two assists, and Toews with two goals.
